chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, my father said to me one day during his illness: 'O my son! Bring some people from the Quraysh, from the inhabitants of Medina, so that I may have them bear witness.' He said: 'So I brought some of them to him, and he said: 'O Ja'far! When I die, wash me, shroud me, and raise my grave four fingers' height, and sprinkle it with water.' So when they went out, I said: 'O father! If you had instructed me with this, I would have done it, and why did you want to bring a group of people to you to bear witness?' So he said: 'O my son! I wanted that there should be no dispute.'

key_terms.أَرْبَعَ أَصَابِعَ: four fingers (a specific measurement for raising the grave)
key_terms.تُنَازَعَ: dispute (specifically regarding inheritance or burial rights)
key_terms.قُرَيْش: Quraysh (the tribe of the Prophet Muhammad)

ai.seo_question: What were Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq's specific instructions for his burial to prevent disputes?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) strategically selected witnesses from the Quraysh of Medina to validate his specific burial rites, ensuring the authenticity of his instructions against potential sectarian disputes. He directed that his grave be raised four fingers above the ground and sprinkled with water, a practice rooted in the Prophetic tradition to distinguish the burial site and honor the deceased, thereby preventing future controversies over his resting place.
